Kutina Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kutina, Croatia

Not demolished. Kutina's Jewish community, organized in 1806, numbered 132 people by 1940, of whom only a few survived the Holocaust. The town's synagogue, designed by the Zagreb architects S. Benedik and A. Baranyai and built in 1914, was abandoned in 1941, confiscated in 1947, and finally demolished in 1969 to make way for a commercial center. This Jewish section of the large municipal cemetery, established in 1873, holds 70 to 80 tombstones in poor, vandalized condition, inscribed in German using Hebrew characters, the oldest dated 1873 and the latest 1926.
